card.name: Words just before complete blood count
card.fires_on: Short words or word starts that come right before an expected medical term, most often "complete" in "complete blood count" (CBC). Also seen before "re" in "reevaluation" and before similar lab or test names.

modes.label: Before complete blood count
modes.description: The word before or at "complete blood count" in lists of lab tests or monitoring.
modes.example: A simple blood test done during a doctor visit, called<< a>> complete blood count or CBC, is used

modes.label: Joining test names
modes.description: A linking word or word start between names of tests or findings, ahead of a second test term.

modes.label: Start of a prefixed word
modes.description: A prefix such as re or un that begins a medical word like reevaluation or unexplained.
modes.example: Continued infection indicates the need for<< re>>evaluation.

card.writes: It suppresses "civil" and similar words, so it steers away from a non-medical reading.
card.plain: It fires on small words just ahead of a test name, especially complete blood count.
